result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.degree_mixing_dict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count edges by the degrees of their two endpoints. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24311-L24365){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.degree_mixing_dict( x="out", y="in", weighted=None, normalized=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Degree mixing dict](/assets/graphs/degree-mixing-dict.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The hub-and-leaf graph with each degree in a badge. The four accent edges join degree 1 to degree 3, and the hub edge C–D joins 3 to 3. Counting every edge from both ends gives {1: {3: 4}, 3: {1: 4, 3: 2}}." width="100%"} For every pair of degrees `(j, k)`, how many edges run from a node of degree `j` to a node of degree `k`. This joint degree distribution is the raw material of degree assortativity: if edges concentrate along `j = k`, similar nodes link to each other. Undirected edges are counted from both ends, so the table is symmetric; on a directed graph each edge is counted once, from its source's `x` degree to its target's `y` degree. See `degree_mixing_matrix()` for the same counts as a matrix. Matches NetworkX's `degree_mixing_dict()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : On directed graphs, the degree of each edge's source: `"out"` (default) or `"in"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["in"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : On directed graphs, the degree of each edge's target: `"in"` (default) or `"out"`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether degrees are weighted (sums of edge weights). If `None` (default), follows the graph. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return fractions of all counted edge ends instead of counts. Default is `False`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A nested dictionary `{j: {k: count}}`. Every degree that appears is a key. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path of four nodes, the two end edges link degree 1 to degree 2, and the middle edge links degree 2 to degree 2: ::: {#3b2e865c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.Graph().add_path_graph(4).degree_mixing_dict() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: {2: 2}, 2: {1: 2, 2: 2}} ``` ::: :::
